info.title: Paessler PRTG
info.description:
Paessler PRTG Network Monitor API provides programmatic access to sensors, devices, groups, monitoring data, and alert management in PRTG.

Authentication: API key in Authorization header — generate a PRTG API token from Setup → Account Settings → My Account → API Token. Pass as Authorization: PrtgSharedSecret <api_token>.

Source: https://www.paessler.com/manuals/prtg/api_overview
info.x-itential-curated: Trimmed to 77 of 115 upstream operations covering common CRUD for automation: Devices, Groups, Probes, and Sensors (create, read, update, delete, pause/resume/scan, clone, autodiscovery), sensor Channels and Timeseries data, and generic Object management (move, count). See the repo README for the full scope and the full spec.

get.description: Get a list of all probes, groups, devices, sensors and channels that match a filter.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Use an offset to define which results the request returns. The index is a zero-based array, which means that the first object has an index of 0. If you have an offset of 0 and a limit of 100, the API returns results 0 to 99. For more information, see the PRTG API v2 Overview: Pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Enter the number of objects that the request returns. If you set the limit to 0 or do not enter a value, the request returns up to 3,000 objects.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Define filters to filter the results. For more information, see the PRTG API v2 Overview: Filters.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
By default, this endpoint only returns the most relevant information about the requested objects. You can include additional parameters: | Parameter | Description | Example | | ------ | ------ | ------ |  | `all_sections`

Individual settings sections | Explicitly request one, multiple, or all settings sections. | `include=all_sections`

`include=intervalgroup,scheduledependency`

`include=path`

| | `inheritance`|Returns information about whether settings are inherited or not. You can only use this parameter together with another parameter. | `include=intervalgroup,inheritance`| |`sensor_status_summary`|Returns the number of sensors on a device grouped by status.|`include=sensor_status_summary`| | `*` | A wildcard that includes the `all_sections`, `inheritance`, and `sensor_status_summary` parameters. | `include=*`| Use the `all_sections` parameter to see all available setting sections. You can then refine your request with the setting sections that you want. For more information, see the [PRTG API v2 Overview: Includes](../overview/index.html#includes).

post.summary: Move the position of any monitoring object within it's siblings or to a new parent.
post.description:
You can either combine `parent` and optionally one of the positional parameter `position`/`position_preset`, if you want to move the object to another parent.
Or if you want to move the object within its siblings you can either use `position` (multiple of 10) or `position_preset`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Enter the ID of the object that you want to move.

parent.description: The new parent where to move the object or 'null'

position.description: The absolute position within the siblings or 'null'.

position_preset.description:
position_preset movement commands or 'null'
  * `top` - move to the first place
  * `bottom` - move to the end
  * `up` - move one place forward
  * `down` - move one place backward

Location.description: Where you can find the moved object

get.summary: Returns time series data of a sensor for predefined time frames.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Enter the ID of the sensor that you want to get the time series data for.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Select the dataset type:

* `live`: Returns data of the last four hours.
* `short`: Returns data of the last 2 days.
* `medium`: Returns data of the last 60 days.
* `long`: Returns data of the last 365 days.

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Enter a comma-separated list of channel IDs that you want to include (e.g. 3074.1, 3074.2) in the response. If left empty, the response includes all channels.

table.description: The first array defines the table headers of the columns. In a time series table, the column headers consist of "time" and all additional channels defined in the 'channels' parameter. Each additional array is a row of data values. In this case, all arrays after the table headers contain the time-date value in RFC3339 format and channel data as an integer or a floating-point number.

get.description: ⚠ Deprecated as of PRTG 24.3.100: This endpoint still works, but will be removed.
get.summary: Get time series data

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Enter the ID of the sensor for which you want to get the time series data.

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Enter the comma separated IDs of the channels you want to include. If left empty all channels will be returned

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The starting point of the sample interval in the past as a timestamp in RFC3339 ("YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ") format.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The ending point of the sample interval in the past as a time stamp in RFC3339 ("YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ") format. If left empty the sample runs up to now.

table.description: The first row is the table header naming the columns. The first column named 'time' contains the timestamp followed by an arbitrary number of columns named by the respective channel IDs. The remaining rows contain the data, timestamps (RFC3339 format) and measurements per channel (integer or floating point number).

CreateRequestBody.title: Create Request Body
CreateRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to create a new object.

AcknowledgeRequestBody.title: Acknowledge Request Body
AcknowledgeRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to acknowledge the alarm of a sensor.

duration.description: Enter the duration of the alarm acknowledgement. Enter zero to  acknowledge the alarm indefinitely. PRTG rounds up the value to full minutes. For example, if you enter 100, PRTG acknowledges the alarm for two minutes.

message.description: Enter a message that the acknowledged sensor displays as a sensor message.

example.message: Alarm acknowledged for five minutes. Troubleshooting in progress.

TriggerAutoDiscoveryRequestBody.title: Trigger Auto Discovery Request Body
TriggerAutoDiscoveryRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to trigger auto discovery for a device. Add the wanted template filenames to the "templates" array. Template filenames for usage can be found in /experimental/devices/templates

Error.title: Error Response
Error.description: This is the schema for all error responses that the API returns.

code.title: The internal API error code. For example, AUTH_FAILED.

message.title: The error message. This provides further information about the error.

request_id.title: The ID of the request that encountered the error.

example.message: The authentication failed. Enter valid credentials.

MultiAcknowledgeRequestBody.title: Multi-Acknowledge Request Body
MultiAcknowledgeRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to acknowledge the alarms of multiple sensors.

filter.description: Define filters to limit and specify the results that the request returns.

duration.description: Enter the duration of the alarm acknowledgement. Enter zero to acknowledge the alarm indefinitely. PRTG rounds up the value to full minutes. For example, if you enter 100, PRTG acknowledges the alarm for two minutes.

message.description: Enter a message that the acknowledged sensor displays as a sensor message.

example.message: Alarms acknowledged for five minutes. Troubleshooting in progress.

MultiPauseRequestBody.title: Multi-Pause Request Body
MultiPauseRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to pause the alarms of multiple sensors.

filter.description: Define filters to limit and specify the results that the request returns.

duration.description: Enter the duration of the alarm acknowledgement. Enter zero to acknowledge the alarm indefinitely. PRTG rounds up the value to full minutes. For example, if you enter 100, PRTG acknowledges the alarm for two minutes.

message.description: Enter a message that the acknowledged sensor displays as a sensor message.

example.message: Alarms acknowledged for five minutes. Troubleshooting in progress.

MultiResumeRequestBody.title: Multi-Resume Request Body
MultiResumeRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to resume multiple objects.

filter.description: Define filters to limit and specify the results that the request returns.

MultiScanNowRequestBody.title: Multi-Scan Now Request Body
MultiScanNowRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to trigger a scan for multiple objects.

filter.description: Define filters to limit the results that the request returns.

PauseRequestBody.title: Action Pause Request Body
PauseRequestBody.description: This is the body of the request to pause a sensor.

duration.description: Enter the duration of the pause. Enter zero to pause the object indefinitely. PRTG rounds up the value to full minutes. For example, if you enter 100, PRTG pauses the object for two minutes.

message.description: Enter a message that the paused sensor displays as sensor message.
